predicted: Week-3 state-of-the-art comparison on the AGGREGATION axis, approved 2026-08-23. BASELINES.md names four directly applicable competitors and only Ditto had been run. FedProx, SCAFFOLD and pFedMe now share one training loop (fedavg_iterative.fed_train) differing ONLY in the local update, and are swapped at the merge boundary via MERGE_MODE, so every policy, oracle and floor downstream is untouched: a difference between modes is a difference in how the shared model was built and nothing else. Five pools at five seeds, matching the existing cut_fa_* FedAvg arm exactly so the four modes are compared on identical decisions. NOTE ON pFedMe: under one-shot merging it coincides with Ditto -- both solve argmin f_i(theta) + (lam/2)||theta - w||^2 against a fixed global w -- so it is run on the iterative axis, where w is updated across rounds and the two genuinely differ. Its personalised model for the target is scored as its own column, ap_pfedme_personal, because evaluating pFedMe on its global model alone would compare it on the one axis it does not claim. PREDICTIONS, from an 8-round 1-seed lendingclub probe (the real runs use 30 rounds). (1) FedProx is within 1 share point of FedAvg on the mean: mu=0.01 is a weak proximal term, participation is full, and the objective is convex, so the proximal pull has little to correct. Probe gave always-merge 0.3057 against FedAvg's 0.3058. (2) SCAFFOLD does NOT beat FedAvg. Control variates correct client drift under partial participation over many rounds; here participation is full. The probe gave 0.3010 against 0.3058, with a LOWER oracle too (0.3256 against 0.3356), which would mean the shared model it builds is worse rather than merely differently tuned. (3) pFedMe's personalised model beats its own global model on every pool; the probe gave 0.3049 against 0.3043. If it does not, our implementation is wrong, since that inequality is what the method is for. (4) None of the three changes the ranking of the DEPLOYABLE policies: adaptive shrinkage stays non-negative against never-merge on every pool above the 0.002 attainable-gain floor. WITHDRAWAL: if any aggregation mode drives blend negative on an above-floor pool, the recommendation in section 6 is mode-dependent and must be stated as such rather than as a property of shrinkage. Report every result ABOVE THE FLOOR with the absolute AUPRC column beside the share, per Results 103-110.
